headline.en: A stave is five lines. Every line and every space is one note, and higher on the stave is higher in pitch. Your do sits where your own note is.

detail.en: Each one is the next note up
Every line here starts on it
Medium volume; stop if anything tightens or hurts

text.en: Watch the stave while it plays, then sing it back: do, re, mi, re, do.
Your turn to read. Look first, then sing it as the notes light: the names are under them.

headline.en: A step goes from a line to the next space, or a space to the next line. Up the stave is up in pitch.

detail.en: Line, space, line: three notes in a row

text.en: Read up to so, names under the notes.
Now back down. The names are faint: read the stave first.

headline.en: Real tunes turn: up a little, back, then on. Follow the notes, not a pattern.

text.en: A line that turns, names faint.
Another, with no names at all.
The treble clef is a fancy letter G. Its curl wraps around the line where G sits, which is why it's also called the G clef.

headline.en: A line you haven't heard, two bars long. Look, find do, then read it straight through.
Do, mi and so are the notes of your home chord. On the stave each sits two steps above the last: line to line, or space to space.

detail.en: Jumps over one line or space

text.en: Watch the skips while they play, then sing them back.
Read the skips, names under the notes.

headline.en: Many tunes start below do, on the so beneath it, and leap up home. On the stave it's a skip and a step lower.

detail.en: So to do, like a call

text.en: So below do, then home: names faint.
Down to so, up through the chord, no names.

headline.en: Now lines mix steps and skips. A step goes to the very next line or space; a skip jumps one.

text.en: The bass clef is a fancy letter F. Its two dots sit either side of the line where F sits, which is why it's also called the F clef.

headline.en: You know this tune by ear. Now read it: Ode to Joy's second line, four bars, from the stave alone.

detail.en: With one dotted note near the end

text.en: Ode to Joy's second line, no names.
